q0273: Craft custom packets to test firewalls = hping. Capture and analyze = Wireshark or tcpdump. Scan ports = nmap.
q0274: Detect data leaving a system (exfiltration) = monitor outbound traffic (egress monitoring, NetFlow anomalies, DLP).
q0275: Prioritize patching by severity score = CVSS, weighed with how critical and exposed each affected asset is.
q0276: An unsupported server that must stay online → place it in a screened subnet (DMZ) between firewalls.
q0277: Reduce the attack surface = remove what is not needed: disable unused services, ports and accounts.
q0278: Real, unspoofed calls from your own numbers that nobody made = your VoIP (SIP) system has been hijacked for toll fraud.
q0279: Printouts left on the printer → print release: the job prints only when the user authenticates at the device.
q0280: Fix file permissions on Linux = chmod (chown changes the owner). /etc/shadow should be readable by root only.
q0281: Printing areas → dumpster diving risk: shred waste and collect printouts promptly.
q0282: Make code hard to reverse engineer or debug = obfuscation.
q0283: Secrets committed to code repositories are the classic accidental credential leak.
q0284: Too many admins with static passwords → a PAM vault: check-out, automatic rotation, just-in-time access and full logging.
q0285: Decoy assets that alert you when someone probes them = honeypot.
q0286: SMS codes can be intercepted (SIM swapping, SS7). TOTP codes are generated on the device and never sent over the network.
q0287: The victim's own logged-in browser tricked into sending a request (such as a password change) = CSRF. Defend with anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies.
q0288: Shadow IT in a cloud-first company with no perimeter → CASB: discover and control cloud app use.
q0289: Malware confirmed on hosts → contain first (isolate them), then eradicate and recover.
q0290: Collect the most volatile evidence first: CPU cache and registers → RAM → swap → disk → logs and archives (order of volatility).
q0291: Step-by-step hardening settings for new devices = secure configuration guide (baseline).
q0292: Keep a card on file safely = tokenization: the real number sits in a vault and systems store a meaningless token.
q0293: Unique local admin passwords on every machine (as LAPS provides) stop one stolen hash from unlocking them all (pass-the-hash).
q0294: Secure command-line file transfer = SFTP (runs over SSH). FTPS is FTP with TLS; plain FTP and Telnet are cleartext.
q0295: Owner = accountable; decides classification and access. Custodian = implements (backups, permissions). Steward = data quality. Controller = GDPR purpose and means.
q0296: Talking through roles in a hypothetical incident = tabletop exercise.
q0297: A company's internal designs, architecture and code = proprietary data (intellectual property).
q0298: A few attempts each against many accounts from one source = password spraying.
q0299: Salting defeats rainbow tables: precomputed hashes no longer match.
q0300: Seamless MFA on personal phones = push notifications. Watch for MFA fatigue; number matching helps.
q0301: Compute on encrypted data without decrypting it = homomorphic encryption: slow, but the provider never sees plaintext.
q0302: Ransomware-resistant backups = offline or immutable copies. Backups on network storage get encrypted along with everything else.
